children.text: ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt
children.translated_text: In the beginning, this was indeed the <s>ātman</s> alone, one only.
Nothing else whatsoever was stirring.

children.text: sa īkṣata lokān nu sṛjā iti ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "Now let me create worlds."

children.text: sa imāṃl lokān asṛjatāmbho marīcīr maram āpaḥ
children.translated_text: He created these worlds: Ambhas, Marīcī, Mara, and the Waters.
That which is Ambhas is beyond heaven.
Heaven is its support.
The mid-space is Marīcī.
The earth is Mara.
Those that are below are the Waters.
He considered, "These then are the worlds.
Now let me create guardians of the worlds."
So from the waters themselves he drew forth a person and shaped him.
He heated him with austerity.
When he had been heated, his mouth split open, like an egg.
From the mouth came speech.
From speech came fire.
The nostrils split open.
From the nostrils came breath.
From breath came wind.
The two eyes split open.
From the eyes came sight.
From sight came the sun.
The two ears split open.
From the ears came hearing.
From hearing came the directions.
The skin split open.
From the skin came the hairs.
From the hairs came herbs and forest trees.
The heart split open.
From the heart came mind.
From mind came the moon.
The navel split open.
From the navel came <s>apāna</s> (downward breath).
From <s>apāna</s> came death.
The generative organ split open.
From the generative organ came seed.
From seed came the waters.

children.text: tā etā devatāḥ sṛṣṭā asmin mahaty arṇave prāpatan
children.translated_text: Those deities, once created, fell into this great ocean.
He subjected that person to hunger and thirst.

children.text: tā enam abruvann āyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi
children.translated_text: They said to him, "Find out an abode for us,
established in which we may eat food."
He brought a cow to them.

children.text: tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti
children.translated_text: They said, "This is certainly not enough for us."
He brought a horse to them.

children.text: tā abruvan na vai no 'yam alam iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "This is certainly not enough for us."
He brought a person to them.
They said, "Ah, this is well made."
For the person is indeed well made.
He said to them, "Enter each according to its own abode."
Fire, becoming speech, entered the mouth.
Wind, becoming breath, entered the nostrils.
The sun, becoming sight, entered the two eyes.
The directions, becoming hearing, entered the two ears.
Herbs and forest trees, becoming hairs, entered the skin.
The moon, becoming mind, entered the heart.
Death, becoming <s>apāna</s>, entered the navel.
The waters, becoming seed, entered the generative organ.
Hunger and thirst said to him, "Provide for us two also."

children.text: te abravīd etāsv eva vāṃ devatāsv ābhajāmy etāsu bhāginyau karomīti
children.translated_text: He said to them, "I assign you two a share in these very deities; I make you two sharers in them."

children.text: tasmād yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havir gṛhyate bhāginyāv evāsyām aśanāpipāse bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for whichever deity an oblation is taken, hunger and thirst become sharers in that deity.

children.text: sa īkṣateme nu lokāś ca lokapālāś ca
children.translated_text: He considered, "These then are the worlds and the guardians of the worlds.
Let me create food for them."
So he heated the waters with austerity.
From those waters, when heated, a form was born.

children.text: yā vai sā mūrtir ajāyatānnaṃ vai tat ||
children.translated_text: The form that was born was indeed food.
That food, once created, tried to flee away from him.
He tried to grasp it with speech.
He could not grasp it with speech.

children.text: sa yaddhainad vācāgrahaiṣyad abhivyāhṛtya haivānnam atrapsyat ||
children.translated_text: If he had grasped it with speech, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by speaking of it.
He tried to grasp it with breath.
He could not grasp it with breath.

children.text: sa yaddhainat prāṇenāgrahaiṣyad abhiprāṇya haivānnam atrapsyat ||
children.translated_text: If he had grasped it with breath, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by breathing toward it.
He tried to grasp it with sight.
He could not grasp it with sight.

children.text: sa yaddhainac cakṣuṣāgrahaiṣyad dṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat ||
children.translated_text: If he had grasped it with sight, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by seeing it.
He tried to grasp it with hearing.
He could not grasp it with hearing.
If he had grasped it with hearing, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by hearing of it.
He tried to grasp it with the skin.
He could not grasp it with the skin.

children.text: sa yaddhainat tvacāgrahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā haivānnam atrapsyat ||
children.translated_text: If he had grasped it with the skin, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by touching it.
He tried to grasp it with the mind.
He could not grasp it with the mind.

children.text: sa yaddhainan manasāgrahaiṣyad dhyātvā haivānnam atrapsyat ||
children.translated_text: If he had grasped it with the mind, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by thinking of it.
He tried to grasp it with the generative organ.
He could not grasp it with the generative organ.
If he had grasped it with the generative organ, then one would have been satisfied with food merely by emitting seed.
He tried to grasp it with <s>apāna</s>.
He took it in.
This, then, is the grasper of food, namely wind.
This wind is indeed the life of food.

children.text: sa īkṣata kathaṃ nv idaṃ mad ṛte syād iti
children.translated_text: He considered, "How could this exist without me?"
He considered, "By which way shall I enter?"

children.text: sa īkṣata yadi vācābhivyāhṛtaṃ yadi prāṇenābhiprāṇitaṃ yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ yadi śrotreṇa śrutaṃ yadi tvacā spṛṣṭaṃ yadi manasā dhyātaṃ yady apānenābhyapānitaṃ yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭam atha ko 'ham iti ||
children.translated_text: He considered, "If speech has spoken, if breath has breathed, if sight has seen, if hearing has heard, if the skin has touched, if the mind has thought, if <s>apāna</s> has breathed downward, if the generative organ has emitted, then who am I?"

children.text: sa etam eva sīmānaṃ vidāryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata
children.translated_text: Splitting open this very seam, he entered by this door.
This door is called the split opening.
That is the place of delight.

children.text: tasya traya āvasathās trayaḥ svapnā ayam āvasatho 'yam āvasatho 'yam āvasatha iti ||
children.translated_text: He has three abodes, three dream-states: this abode, this abode, and this abode.

children.text: sa jāto bhūtāny abhivyaikhyat kim ihānyaṃ vāvadiṣad iti
children.translated_text: Once born, he looked over beings, thinking, "What else here would one wish to speak of?"

children.text: sa etam eva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamam apaśyad idam adarśam ||
children.translated_text: He saw this very person as the most pervasive <s>brahman</s>: "I have seen this."
Therefore his name is <s>Idandra</s>.
Indeed his name is <s>Idandra</s>.

children.text: tam idandraṃ santam indra ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa
children.translated_text: Though he is <s>Idandra</s>, they call him <s>Indra</s> indirectly.

children.text: parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the gods seem to love what is indirect; the gods indeed seem to love what is indirect.

children.text: puruṣe ha vā ayam ādito garbho bhavati yad etad retaḥ
children.translated_text: In a man, indeed, this first becomes an embryo, namely this seed.

children.text: tad etat sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyas tejaḥ sambhūtam ātmany evātmānaṃ bibharti
children.translated_text: This seed, formed as the essence from all the limbs, bears itself as self within the self.

children.text: tad yadā striyāṃ siñcaty athainaj janayati
children.translated_text: When he pours it into a woman, then he generates it.
That is his first birth.

children.text: tat striyā ātmabhūyaṃ gacchati yathā svam aṅgaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: That goes into the woman, becoming her self, just like her own limb.
Therefore she does not harm it.
She nourishes this self of his that has entered there.
She, as the nourisher, becomes one who is to be nourished.
The woman bears that embryo.
He, from the very beginning, before birth, nourishes the boy.

children.text: sa yat kumāraṃ janmano 'gre 'dhi bhāvayaty ātmānam eva tad bhāvayaty eṣāṃ lokānāṃ santatyai
children.translated_text: In that he nourishes the boy before birth, he thereby nourishes himself, for the continuity of these worlds.
For in this way these worlds are continued.
That is his second birth.
This self of his is entrusted to meritorious actions.

children.text: athāsyāyam itara ātmā kṛtakṛtyo vayogataḥ praiti
children.translated_text: Then this other self of his, having done what was to be done and grown old, departs.

children.text: sa itaḥ prayann eva punar jāyate
children.translated_text: Departing from here, he is born again.
That is his third birth.

children.text: tad uktam ṛṣiṇā garbhe nu sann anv eṣām avedam ahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā
children.translated_text: That was spoken by the seer: While still in the womb I knew all these births of the gods.

children.text: śataṃ mā pura āyasīr arakṣannadha śyeno javasā nir adīyam
children.translated_text: A hundred iron fortresses guarded me; then, like a hawk, I flew out swiftly.
So it is said.
While lying in the womb, <s>Vāmadeva</s> spoke thus.

children.text: sa evaṃ vidvān asmāccharīrabhedād ūrdhvam utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmān āptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat ||
children.translated_text: Knowing thus, after the breaking of this body he rose upward from here, and in that heavenly world, having obtained all desires, he became immortal, he became immortal.
Who is this one?
It is the <s>ātman</s> (self) that we worship.
Which one is that <s>ātman</s>?

children.text: yena vā paśyati yena vā śṛṇoti yena vā gandhāñjighrati yena vā vācaṃ vyākaroti yena vā svādu cāsvādu ca vijānāti ||
children.translated_text: That by which one sees, by which one hears, by which one smells odors, by which one articulates speech, and by which one knows what is sweet and not sweet.
That which is this heart and mind: this is it.

children.text: saṃjñānam ājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ medhā dṛṣṭir dhṛtir matir manīṣā jūtiḥ smṛtiḥ saṅkalpaḥ kratur asuḥ kāmo vaśa iti sarvāṇy evaitāni prajñānasya nāmadheyāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness, command, discernment, insight, intelligence, vision, steadfastness, thought, reflection, impulse, memory, intention, resolve, life-breath, desire, and control: all these are indeed names of <s>prajñāna</s> (conscious awareness).
This is <s>Brahmā</s>.
This is <s>Indra</s>.
This is <s>Prajāpati</s>.
These are all the gods.

children.text: imāni ca pañca mahābhūtāni pṛthivī vāyur ākāśa āpo jyotīṃṣīty etānīmāni kṣudramiśrāṇīva bījānītarāṇi cetarāṇi cāṇḍajāni ca jārujāni ca svedajāni codbhijjāni cāśvā gāvaḥ puruṣā hastino yat kiñcedam prāṇi jaṅgamaṃ ca patatri ca yac ca sthāvaram
children.translated_text: And these five great elements, earth, wind, space, waters, and lights; these small mixed things as it were, seeds of various kinds; those born from eggs, born from wombs, born from sweat, and born from shoots; horses, cows, human beings, elephants, whatever living thing there is, moving and flying, and whatever is stationary.
All that has <s>prajñāna</s> as its guiding eye.
It is established in <s>prajñāna</s>.
The world has <s>prajñāna</s> as its guiding eye.
<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom-consciousness) is the foundation.
<s>Prajñāna</s> (consciousness) is <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: sa etena prajñenātmanāsmāl lokād utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmān āptvāmṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat ||
children.translated_text: With this conscious self he rose up from this world, and in that heavenly world, having obtained all desires, he became immortal, he became immortal.
